key_insight: A multimodal cardiac foundation model pretrained on signals and clinical text from ~1.7 million people provides reliable, device-agnostic cardiac assessment across hospital-grade and consumer wearable data. It unifies diverse heart-signal formats to produce consistent clinical insights.
problem_solved: Heterogeneity of cardiac data across devices and settings (hospital ECGs vs. home wearables) and the lack of large, unified models that generalize across formats, limiting deployment and consistency of AI-driven cardiac assessment.
method: Assemble a large multimodal corpus of heart signals paired with textual interpretations from ~1.7M individuals to capture diverse devices and settings.
Pretrain a foundation model that jointly represents signal and language modalities to learn generalizable cardiac representations.
Apply the pretrained model to downstream tasks (diagnosis, monitoring, cross-device inference) with minimal task-specific adaptation to ensure broad applicability.
impact: Enables AI/ML teams to build robust cardiac tools that generalize across device types and care settings, reducing the need for device-specific retraining and accelerating safe deployment in clinics and consumer health. Supports scalable development of monitoring, triage, and diagnostic applications.
